lessons.goal: 重讀句子找出限制語與相對應詞義。

questions.evidence: At the review table, students read five sentences from a pretend cafe guide. Each sentence contains a blank. The word cards are discount, average, nearby, reserved, and remain. Students may use each card once, so every choice must fit its own sentence.
questions.explanation: 規則限定每張卡只能使用一次。
questions.prompt: How many times may each card be used?

questions.evidence: The teacher asks each pair to name a clue, not just a translation. Kai circles less than usual on his sheet. He writes that rereading one useful phrase can be faster than guessing several unrelated words.
questions.explanation: 末段說他圈出 less than usual。

questions.evidence: Kai quickly puts average into a sentence about tea costing less than usual. Mei asks him to compare the sentence with the week's price notice. Kai changes his choice to discount and saves average for a sentence about three trial distances.
questions.explanation: 回想本週價格公告可辨認折扣語意。
options: It proves trial distances cannot be averaged.
It says all tables cost the same.
It provides a familiar context for discount.
It gives the final answer to every sentence.
questions.prompt: Why does Mei mention the price notice?

questions.evidence: Another sentence says a table is being held for a group arriving later. The pair chooses reserved. A toilet a short walk away is nearby. In the final sentence, only two cups are still on the shelf, so two cups remain.
questions.explanation: 桌子為稍後抵達的特定團體保留。

questions.evidence: Another sentence says a table is being held for a group arriving later. The pair chooses reserved. A toilet a short walk away is nearby. In the final sentence, only two cups are still on the shelf, so two cups remain.
questions.explanation: 第三段對 nearby 與 remain 各有明確語境。
options: Reserved—costing less; nearby—still on the shelf.
Remain—a short walk; discount—a future group.
Nearby—a short walk; remain—still on the shelf.
questions.prompt: Which two matches fit the review?

lessons.story:
At the review table, students read five sentences from a pretend cafe guide. Each sentence contains a blank. The word cards are discount, average, nearby, reserved, and remain. Students may use each card once, so every choice must fit its own sentence.

Kai quickly puts average into a sentence about tea costing less than usual. Mei asks him to compare the sentence with the week's price notice. Kai changes his choice to discount and saves average for a sentence about three trial distances.

Another sentence says a table is being held for a group arriving later. The pair chooses reserved. A toilet a short walk away is nearby. In the final sentence, only two cups are still on the shelf, so two cups remain.

The teacher asks each pair to name a clue, not just a translation. Kai circles less than usual on his sheet. He writes that rereading one useful phrase can be faster than guessing several unrelated words.
lessons.title: Five Words at the Cafe
